history.new: In substance - Kurth's criteria A and D (W. Kurth, dissertation, TU Clausthal 1990, who treated all length-increasing one-rule systems with |r| <= 6), McNaughton's barren criterion and Zantema-Geser Thm 1.1, as stated in A. Geser, J. Waldmann, M. Wenzel, Symbolic enumeration of one-rule string rewriting systems, WST 2016, section 4; the census itself was not found as a statement (Historian audit 2026-10-18, reviews/historian_C03_C10.md).
history.old: A small exhaustive census; termination of one-rule systems is a classical topic (Zantema-Geser, Dershowitz "Open. Closed. Open.", RTA 2005) and this observation is likely folklore.

proof_check: computer-assisted (Python) - explicit termination certificates (length decrease, lexicographic monotonicity, linear interpretations over N, decreasing factor counts) for 162 rules and self-embeddings for 34, all re-checked independently
statement:
Among the 196 rules l -> r over {a,b} with 1 <= |l| <= 3, 0 <= |r| <= 3, l != r, exactly the 34 rules in
which l is a factor of r are non-terminating; the other 162 terminate.
title: Termination census of one-rule systems with |l|, |r| <= 3: non-terminating iff l is a factor of r
